title: Two coins: why two heads is only 1 in 4
examples: What is the probability of getting two heads?
Why is two heads 1 in 4 and not 1 in 3?
What is the probability of one head and one tail?

explain.say: Toss two coins. Many people think there are 3 results: two heads, two tails, or one of each. So two heads would be 1 in 3. But that is a trap! Look at the board.

explain.say: Look at the first group. The first coin lands heads. Then the second coin can be heads or tails. That gives two results.

groups.label: First coin tails

explain.say: Now the first coin lands tails. Again, the second can be heads or tails. So there are 4 results in total, all equally likely. How many of them are two heads?

explain.say: Just one! So the probability of two heads is 1 out of 4, a quarter. Look at the bar: 1 part out of 4.

Great thinking! One head and one tail can happen 2 ways: heads then tails, or tails then heads. So it is 2 out of 4, a half. Wow: listing outcomes like this helps scientists predict traits in families. Challenge: what is the chance of two sixes with two dice?

faq.a: Each coin has 2 ways to land, and 2 times 2 is 4: heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads and tails-tails.
asks: How many outcomes do two coins have?

faq.q: Why is two heads not 1 in 3?
faq.a: One of each can happen in 2 different ways, so the 3 results are not equally likely. Listing all 4 equally likely results shows two heads is 1 in 4.

faq.q: What is the probability of one head and one tail?
faq.a: It happens 2 ways out of 4, heads-tails or tails-heads, so the probability is one half.
asks: Probability of a head and a tail

faq.a: For two separate events, multiply their probabilities. Heads then heads is one half times one half, which is one quarter.

faq.q: What is the chance of two sixes?
faq.a: One sixth times one sixth is one thirty-sixth. Out of 36 equally likely pairs, only one is double six.

facts: Two coins have 4 equally likely outcomes: HH, HT, TH and TT.
Two dice have 36 equally likely outcomes, so a double six has probability 1/36.

quiz.say: You toss two coins. What is the probability of two tails?
quiz.why: Two tails is 1 of the 4 equally likely outcomes.

wrong.1: One third counts only 3 results, but one of each happens 2 ways.
wrong.2: One half is the chance for one coin, not both.

quiz.say: You toss two coins. What is the probability of at least one head?
quiz.why: HH, HT and TH all have a head: 3 out of 4.

wrong.1: One half forgets the two heads result.
wrong.2: One quarter is the chance of no heads at all.
